dedupe_keys.name: zindi unicef and arm flood prediction flooded fraction of about 1 km cells in southern malawi for the 2015 floods and cyclone idai 2019

description: UNICEF Arm 2030 Vision #1: Flood Prediction in Malawi was a Zindi challenge (December 2019 to May 2020) on predicting the location and extent of floods in southern Malawi. Contents: southern Malawi divided into roughly 1 km square cells, each with a target giving the fraction of the cell flooded in the 2015 floods (training) and in the March 2019 Cyclone Idai floods (test), plus starter features per cell: mean elevation, dominant land cover type and weekly precipitation for 18 weeks around each event. The Lower Shire Valley districts of Chikwawa and Nsanje are named as the most flood-prone area. Producer: Zindi with UNICEF and Arm under the 2030Vision initiative. Coverage: southern Malawi, events of about 13 January 2015 and 14 March 2019. Format and access: Train.csv, a data archive and sample submission from Zindi after joining. Licence: the pages read do not state a data licence; use follows the competition rules. Caveats: two events only, and the flood extents come from an unnamed source on the pages read. Simulation uses: flood extent modelling and exposure of roads, settlements and health facilities in the Shire valley, and testing flood susceptibility models. Related records: data-malawi-health-facilities-registry-dhis2 and case_study-malawi-restore-road-reconstruction-and-climate-risk-assessment-after-cyclone-freddy.
